criticHypotheses.text: (a) the leaf material has no transmission/subsurface term at all, so a thin leaf is shaded as an opaque Lambert sheet
criticHypotheses.status: DISPROVED. FRAGMENT_SSS has existed for several rounds and both bamboo materials call it with non-zero uSSSStrength — 0.80 on bamboo-plant, 1.15 on bamboo-card, with uSSSFloor 0.22 / 0.34. The term is present, linked and evaluated.

criticHypotheses.text: (b) transmission exists but is being evaluated against the wrong light or clamped out at this sun elevation
criticHypotheses.status: BOTH HALVES DISPROVED, and the real mechanism found underneath them. WRONG LIGHT: at the `valley` pose (Cinematic.js SHOTS.valley eye 34.4,2.3,30.6 -> target 186.47,-22.07,158.2) the view axis is (0.760,-0.122,0.638) and sun.dir from the r16v1 report is (0.86,0.225,0.457), so dot(V,-uSunDir) = 0.918 and `forward` = 0.846 — the lobe is evaluated against the right light and is at 85% of its maximum. CLAMPED OUT: the ceiling is min(through*trans, 0.85) and the shipped product's largest channel was 0.0291, i.e. 29x under the clamp. Nothing is clipping.
criticHypotheses.note: The critic's suggested ablation — 'force a transmission term to a large value and re-measure' — would NOT have found this. uSSSStrength scales a colour that is already wrong; raising it makes the sea a brighter bottle-green.

mechanism.conclusion: The leaf tint is applied TWICE along the transmission path, so the transmitted light is the leaf colour SQUARED. That annihilates red and makes a backlit bamboo sea physically incapable of going warm at any strength.
mechanism.where: FRAGMENT_SSS. `trans = mix(vec3(1), uSSSColor, uSSSSat) * uSunColor * ...` and `through = mix(diffuseColor.rgb, uSSSColor * (0.26 + aLum*1.9), uSSSFloor)`, then `glow = min(through * trans, 0.85)`. uSSSColor appears in both factors.
arithmetic: bamboo-card shipped r16: uSSSColor 0x3fb520, uSSSSat 1.0, uSSSFloor 0.34, uSSSStrength 1.15. Three converts the hex through sRGB, so C_lin = (0.0497, 0.4508, 0.0144).
At uSSSSat 1.0 the tint is not desaturated at all, so the squared factor is 0.0497^2 = 0.00247 in red against 0.4508^2 = 0.2032 in green — a ratio of 82:1 BEFORE the albedo is consulted.

Evaluated on the sheet's own literal leaf colour rgb(66,148,52) at shade 0.85 (paintBambooClump's mass pass), with uSunColor (1, 0.412, 0.134) from the r16v1 report and forward 0.846: trans = (0.0337, 0.1291, 0.0013), through = (0.0357, 0.2255, 0.0195), glow = (0.0012, 0.0291, 0.00003). R/G 0.041, blue gone entirely.

Same evaluation over a population-weighted texel set (40% mass rgb(66,148,52), 22% deep mass rgb(34,88,30), 20% blade rgb(102,194,74), 18% pale culm rgb(138,164,92), all at shade 0.85, plus a hemisphere-ambient diffuse term): surface radiance R/G 0.107 and luminance 0.0313.

With the tint applied ONCE (uSSSSat 0.12, uSSSColor 0xa8c845, uSSSStrength 1.40, uSSSFloor 0.36) the same population gives R/G ~1.04 and luminance x2.8-2.9. Per texel the glow R/G moves 0.041 -> 0.89 (mass), 0.036 -> 1.03 (deep mass), 0.053 -> 0.92 (blade), 0.121 -> 1.52 (pale culm).
mechanism.whyItMatters: This is the same defect class as 'albedo multiplied by itself' in HANDOFF.md's list, wearing different clothes. It is silent: the uniforms all read plausibly, the term is linked, the light is right, nothing is clamped, and the only symptom is that the one shot ARCHITECTURE §9's SUN_AZIMUTH_DEFAULT exists to serve cannot fire.

cards: Card height is h = (7.0 + 9.0*rF) * spec.hScale * (0.82 + rnd*0.36) with rF = clamp((r-96)/150, 0, 1) and hScale in {1.14, 1.00, 0.92, 0.72}. At r = 130 that is 9.04 m base, 12.2 m at the extreme; at r = 170, 11.4 m base and 15.4 m at the extreme.

Ground from core's own r16 ray-march: 779.7 m at r = 130 and about 759 m at r = 170 (interpolating its 691.8 at 300). So the tallest card top is 791.9 m at r = 130 and 774.4 m at r = 170, i.e. 26.1 m and 43.6 m BELOW the new eye at 818.00.

The new pose's pitch is atan(-24.37 / 198.5) = -7.0 deg and fov 44, so the frame spans +15.0 to -29.0 deg. Those card tops sit at atan(26.1/18) = 55.4 deg and atan(43.6/58) = 36.9 deg below horizontal — both BELOW the bottom of the frame.
Cards nearer than 23 m from the camera are also inside fadeIn(RANGE.bambooCard) = [23, 29] and are dissolving, which covers r < 135 on the view bearing.

regressionIntroducedAndFixed.severity: BLOCKER, self-inflicted, introduced by my own commit 0f5dc48 and fixed here. The whole foliage system was absent from every frame of r17v1.
regressionIntroducedAndFixed.mechanism: A temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError in paintBlossom, thrown on the first floret of the first call, i.e. inside _buildTextures, which is step 1 of FoliageSystem.init().
regressionIntroducedAndFixed.exactFault: I introduced a function-scoped `const k` at the top of paintBlossom (the floret radius scale derived from BLOSSOM_CARD_M) and then referenced it at `const r = size * (...) * k;` INSIDE the floret loop. That loop body already declared its own `const k = 0.90 + rnd() * 0.16;` four lines further down. A `const` shadows for its ENTIRE block, not from its declaration onward, so the reference resolved to the inner binding in its temporal dead zone and threw `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'k' before initialization` every single time. It was never conditional on BLOSSOM_CARD_M, which is why the coordinator's bisect A — reverting the 0.92 gate flip to 2.68 — correctly exonerated that edit.
regressionIntroducedAndFixed.fix: Renamed the two derived constants so they cannot be shadowed: `k` -> `floretScale`, `L` -> `layoutK`. No arithmetic changed; floretScale/florets/layoutK are still 2.481 / 12 / 0.473 at BLOSSOM_CARD_M 0.92 and 1.000 / 72 / 1.000 at 2.68. Nothing else in the round-17 work was dropped: the SSS double-tint fix, leafFrom 0.26, sprays 20, internodes 6 and alphaTest 0.22 are all kept.
regressionIntroducedAndFixed.whyItGotThroughReview: `node --check` parses and cannot see a TDZ — it is a runtime error, and I treated a clean parse as evidence the file would boot. That was the whole gap: I measured pixels and triangles carefully and never once executed the code. The rule this project already has — 'configuration that looks correct is not evidence' — applies to a diff as much as to a uniform.

theSwallower.where: src/main.js:168-179, the boot loop. Each system runs inside `try { await fn(); } catch (err) { console.error(`[boot] system "${key}" failed`, err); if (key === 'materials' || key === 'sky' || key === 'terrain') throw err; }`. `foliage` is not in that essential set, so the boot continues and `window.__kagerouReady` is still set: booted reads true and the capture proceeds against a build with no foliage in it.
theSwallower.whyEVERYTHING vanished rather than part: Two compounding facts. (1) `FoliageSystem.init()` does `this.ctx.scene.add(this.group)` at the very END, after all thirteen steps, so a throw at ANY step orphans every resource built before it — the group is never parented and not one mesh can draw. (2) `engine.add(ctx.foliage)` in main.js runs after `await ctx.foliage.init()`, so the system is never even updated. `ctx.foliage` is nevertheless assigned (the constructor ran), so every `ctx.foliage?.x` consumer downstream sees a live-looking object on a half-built system and reports nothing.
theSwallower.theInferenceThatWasWrong: The coordinator read `level:static:0,0:__blossom` still drawing at 31,140 triangles as proof that my texture library had built and the abort was later. It is not: `this.blossomTexture = this.tex.blossom` is assigned AFTER the `this.tex = { ... }` object literal in _buildTextures, so the throw inside that literal leaves blossomTexture null and Props draws the merged canopy geometry on its material's base colour. The abort was in fact in the FIRST step, not a late one. Worth recording because the same inference will be made again.

apparatusFinding.claim: A real `console.error` WAS emitted for this failure and the r17v1 report does not contain it. The round's 'no non-warning console errors' clearance was false, and that is a rig defect independent of my bug.
apparatusFinding.evidence: tools/capture.mjs:305 pushes every console message of type error or warning into `logs`, and line 690 writes `errors: logs.slice(0, 40)`. shots/report-r17v1.json profiles.phone.errors has 17 entries — 12 Canvas2D willReadFrequently warnings, 4 GL ReadPixels stalls and 1 requestFullscreen warning — so the 40-cap did not truncate anything, and the string `[boot] system "foliage" failed` is not among them. The listener is attached before page.goto, so ordering is not the explanation.
apparatusFinding.corroboration: The 12 Canvas2D warnings are themselves the fingerprint of where the throw landed. Chrome emits that warning once per canvas context that does a readback, and counting the canvases _buildTextures touches before `blossom:` in its object literal (clump, the four tussock cells plus the strip, the bamboo-plant sheet plus its leaf sub-canvas, the four bamboo-card cells plus the atlas) gives 12-14. paintBlossom throws before its own canvas is ever read back, so the count stops exactly at the blossom entry.
apparatusFinding.askOfTheRig: Either surface `errors` in the round gate, or fail the gate when drawsByOwner loses an owner that was present in the previous round. A whole system disappearing should not need a human to notice a missing key. This project has now lost rounds twice to silently-absent foliage — 11,390 bamboo cards whose shader linked dead, and this.

verificationByConstruction.method: No capture and no browser was launched. I wrote a Node harness that stubs Canvas2D with pure no-ops (getImageData/createImageData return correctly-sized zeroed buffers, gradients are addColorStop no-ops, every unlisted 2D call is a no-op via a Proxy) plus a stub ctx (three.js Scene/Camera, a renderer with the handful of methods _bakeImpostors calls, Weather's two wind uniforms, and a terrain shaped to core's own r16 ray-march: 812.0 at r<=80, 779.7 at 130, 691.8 at 300). No shim value can change a branch, so anything that throws throws for a structural reason. Then it constructs FoliageSystem and awaits init().
